1.title: Decoupling and Event-Driven Integration
1.text: Welcome to Module one: Decoupling and Event-Driven Integration. It covers the exam area Domain one: Development with A W S Services. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Identify tightly and loosely coupled systems and decouple components (one point one.one). Choose between synchronous and asynchronous patterns (one point one.two). Implement event-driven patterns with Event Bridge, S three event notifications, S Q S and S N S (one point one.eight). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Domain one: Development with A W S Services (thirty percent). Exam format: fifty scored questions, multiple choice and multiple response; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A W S Developer Associate (D V A-C three) exam guide.

1.title: Tight and loose coupling
1.text: Tight and loose coupling. Tightly coupled. What it means: A component calls another directly and waits; both must be up and fast. Risk or benefit: One slow or failed part breaks the chain. Loosely coupled. What it means: Components talk through a queue, topic or event bus; each can fail, scale and change on its own. Risk or benefit: Absorbs spikes, hides failures, easier to change. A W S gives you three decoupling services: Amazon S Q S (queue), Amazon S N S (publish and subscribe topic) and Amazon Event Bridge (event bus with rules). A W S Step Functions coordinates multi-step workflows.

1.title: Synchronous or asynchronous
1.text: Synchronous or asynchronous. The figure shows this: Synchronous request-response compared with asynchronous queue and event flows.

1.title: Synchronous or asynchronous, continued
1.text: Synchronous or asynchronous. Synchronous. Example: A P I Gateway calls Lambda; the client waits for the answer. Use when: The caller needs the result now. Asynchronous with a queue. Example: App puts a message in S Q S; a worker processes it later. Use when: Spiky load, work can wait, you want retries. Asynchronous with events. Example: Event Bridge routes an event to targets. Use when: Many consumers react to a fact that happened. Exam tip: "The user must see the result immediately" equals synchronous. "Absorb traffic spikes" or "process later" equals a queue.

1.title: Amazon SQS
1.text: Amazon S Q S. Standard queue. At-least-once delivery, best-effort ordering, nearly unlimited throughput. F I F O queue. Exactly-once processing, strict order within a message group I D. Visibility timeout. After a consumer receives a message it is hidden for this time (default thirty seconds); if not deleted in time it reappears. Long polling. Wait Time Seconds up to twenty reduces empty responses and cost. Dead-letter queue (D L Q). Messages that fail max Receive Count times move here for study. Retention. Default four days, up to fourteen days. A consumer must delete a message after it succeeds. Make processing idempotent, because standard queues can deliver a message more than once. limits such as message size.

1.title: Amazon SNS
1.text: Amazon S N S. S N S is publish and subscribe: one topic, many subscribers (S Q S, Lambda, H T T P, email, S M S). Fan-out equals publish once to S N S, deliver to several S Q S queues. Subscription filter policies let each subscriber receive only the messages it needs.

1.title: Amazon EventBridge and S3 events
1.text: Amazon Event Bridge and S three events. Event Bridge. Event bus that matches events with rules and event patterns and sends them to targets (Lambda, S Q S, Step Functions and more); also scheduled rules and Scheduler. S three Event Notifications. S three emits an event (object created, removed) to Lambda, S Q S, S N S or Event Bridge. Exam tip: S N S equals push to many. S Q S equals pull by one consumer group. Event Bridge equals route by content, many A W S and sass sources. Exam tip: Standard S Q S can deliver a message more than once, so the consumer must be idempotent; F I F O is the choice for ordering and exactly-once processing.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A web app sends orders to a payment service that is sometimes slow, so the whole checkout fails. What change best decouples them? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Put the orders on an Amazon S Q S queue that the payment service reads. A queue absorbs the load and lets each side fail and scale on its own.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. One upload to S three must trigger a thumbnail Lambda, a metadata Lambda and an audit queue. Which design fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: S three event notification to an S N S topic with the three targets subscribed. Fan-out through S N S delivers one event to many subscribers.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A consumer sometimes crashes after receiving a message and the message is processed twice. What should the developer do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Make the processing idempotent and delete the message after success. At-least-once delivery means a message can arrive again, so processing must be idempotent.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Messages that always fail keep returning to the queue. Which feature isolates them for later study? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A dead-letter queue. A D L Q receives messages that exceed max Receive Count.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An application must process orders in the exact order per customer and exactly once. Which queue type fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: F I F O queue with the customer I D as message group I D. F I F O preserves order within a message group and processes exactly once.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A team wants to route events from many A W S services by their content to different targets. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Amazon Event Bridge. Event Bridge matches events against rules and event patterns and sends them to targets.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the default S Q S visibility timeout? Answer: thirty seconds. Question two. What does a F I F O queue guarantee? Answer: Exactly-once processing and ordering within a message group I D. Question three. What does long polling do? Answer: It waits up to twenty seconds for messages, reducing empty responses and cost.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is S N S fan-out? Answer: Publishing once to a topic that delivers to several subscribers, often several S Q S queues. Question five. Name two targets of an S three event notification. Answer: For example Lambda, S Q S, S N S or Event Bridge. Question six. Which services decouple application components? Answer: S Q S, S N S and Event Bridge (with Step Functions for workflows).

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Coupling: tight equals direct call and wait; loose equals queue, topic or bus. S Q S: standard (at-least-once) versus F I F O (exactly-once, ordered); visibility timeout; D L Q; long polling. S N S: publish and subscribe, fan-out, filter policies. Event Bridge: rules and event patterns to targets. Idempotency: required with at-least-once delivery.
